messages:
Jamal (AE): Hey team — NordBank wants a POC to migrate off VendorX to Redwood. Main asks: prompt parity, token billing differences, security questionnaire, and an integration checklist. Can SE + Eng owners weigh in?

Ana (Sales Eng): I can own the SE side. Quick checklist to start: 1) API surface mapping, 2) prompt/response parity tests, 3) billing delta estimation, 4) security & network Qs, 5) canary rollout plan.

Maya (Eng Lead): For API mapping: VendorX has a nested `payload` -> `messages` array and a custom `session_id` header. Redwood's API uses the standard messages array but function-calling shapes differ. We'll probably need a tiny adapter.

Ana (Sales Eng): Example mismatch we saw before:
```
VendorX request: {
  "payload": {
    "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"..."}, {"role":"user","content":"..."}]},
  "session_id": "abc123"
}
Redwood request: {
  "model": "rwd-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"..."}, {"role":"user","content":"..."}]
}
```
We can do a trivial shim that pulls payload.messages and maps headers.

Kevin (NordBank Eng): Token billing concerns: VendorX charges per chunked token differently. Will switching to Redwood increase cost? Need an estimate for our typical 6k-character prompts + 3-6 exchanges/session.

Ana (Sales Eng): We can run a cost preview. Need a sample traffic trace or representative prompt set. If they commit to dedicated capacity we can offer reserved pricing which usually beats pay-as-you-go for sustained load.

Maya (Eng Lead): Technical caveats to call out for parity tests: 1) KV-cache/session semantics — VendorX pins conversation state in session_id; Redwood uses explicit context or stateful session API. 2) Streaming chunk boundaries differ — affects UX if frontend expects flush points. 3) Function-calling edge cases — vendor defaults to returning first-best candidate, we return top-n depending on params. We should include an eval harness to detect behavioral deltas.

Rohan (Security Ops): Send them our standard security questionnaire (link below) and ask for VendorX PCA / logs they're willing to share. Key asks from our side: SSO (Okta) support + SCIM, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), encryption at rest, egress restrictions, SOC2 report, recent pen test. Also: do they need on-prem Private deployment or VPC peering?

Rohan (Security Ops): Security questionnaire: https://redwood.internal/sec-qa (please attach to the thread once they've filled)

Kevin (NordBank Eng): We need KMS/HSM support, and egress IP allowlist for our internal services. Also, legal will ask about data residency (EU-only).

Maya (Eng Lead): KMS + HSM: Redwood supports CMK via cloud KMS; HSM can be discussed under Private deployment. Data residency: we can pin deployment region for Dedicated/Private.

Ana (Sales Eng): Proposed POC timeline (2 weeks):
- Day 0: Kickoff + get sample prompts/traffic
- Day 2: Adapter shim + basic auth mapping done
- Day 4: Smoke tests (latency, errors)
- Day 7: Parity evals with prompt sets (automated diff)
- Day 10: Security review & questionnaire responses
- Day 14: Canary run + go/no-go discussion

Maya (Eng Lead): For parity evals, we need: a) ~100 representative prompts, b) acceptance thresholds (BLEU-like or custom match rules), c) vendor outputs if available. We can run A/B and show percentage delta.

Jamal (AE): Commercials question: if they move to Dedicated with reserved capacity do we have a standard true-up and discount schedule? Also, any migration credits we can offer to offset initial adapter work?

Ana (Sales Eng): Yes — standard reserved-capacity discounts apply. We can package a short-term migration credit for integration engineering hours; I'll propose a $10k integration credit for deals that commit 12+ months.

infra-bot: canary cluster created: canary-57 (region: eu-west-1)

Rohan (Security Ops): One more item: rotation windows for CMK and audit log retention. Also request copy of VendorX's retention policy to aid legal.

Kevin (NordBank Eng): I'll get the prompt set and a 72-hour traffic dump. Also I'll ask legal to fill the questionnaire and ping back. Timeline looks good.

Jamal (AE): Great — Ana, Maya: can you confirm resources for Day 2 shim and Day 7 parity evals? If so I'll lock the kickoff for next Tuesday.

Ana (Sales Eng): I can take Day 2 and Day 7.

Maya (Eng Lead): Eng team can allocate a 0.5 FTE for the two-week window. Need access to their VendorX logs by Monday.

Jamal (AE): Perfect. I'll set calendar invites and add the security questionnaire to the handoff pack. Thanks all :thumbsup:
